summary: The XRD and NPD analyses across multiple figures demonstrate that mechanochemically synthesized CsPbBr3 adopts an orthorhombic (Pbnm) structure at room temperature and below, with a clear phase transition to a cubic (Pm-3m) structure at elevated temperatures. The structure is well-crystallized, with sharp diffraction peaks and refined lattice parameters. The phase transition is evidenced by merging and sharpening of peaks and is accompanied by changes in unit-cell parameters and volume.
experimental_variables: diffraction technique (laboratory XRD, synchrotron XRD, neutron powder diffraction)

key_findings.finding: CsPbBr3 synthesized by mechanochemical methods is phase-pure and adopts the orthorhombic Pbnm structure at room temperature and below, as confirmed by both laboratory XRD and NPD/SXRD (Le Bail and Rietveld refinements).
The orthorhombic structure persists down to 4 K, with refined lattice parameters at 4 K: a = 7.9734 Å, b = 8.3065 Å, c = 11.612 Å, V = 769.1 Å³ (Pbnm).
A reversible phase transition from orthorhombic (Pbnm) to cubic (Pm-3m) occurs between 298 K and 473 K, as shown by the merging and sharpening of peaks and the change in symmetry in SXRD patterns.
Above 473 K, CsPbBr3 remains cubic (Pm-3m) up to at least 773 K, with increasing peak intensity and no evidence of further phase transitions.

scientific_interpretation: The combined XRD and NPD results establish that mechanochemical synthesis yields highly crystalline, phase-pure CsPbBr3 with an orthorhombic structure at ambient and low temperatures. The observed phase transition to a cubic structure upon heating is consistent across both synchrotron and laboratory data, indicating robust structural evolution with temperature. The sharpness of the peaks and the quality of the Rietveld fits suggest good crystallinity and minimal disorder. The thermal evolution of lattice parameters and unit-cell volume (fig_3, fig_7) further supports the structural transition and provides quantitative insight into the anisotropic thermal expansion and symmetry change. No evidence of secondary phases or decomposition is observed within the studied temperature range.
limitations: No explicit quantitative phase fraction analysis is provided for the phase transition region; the exact transition temperature is bracketed but not pinpointed.
Lattice parameters for the cubic phase at high temperature are not reported in the extracted data.
No information is given about possible hysteresis or reversibility of the phase transition upon cooling.
Peak intensities and widths are described qualitatively; no microstructural analysis (e.g., crystallite size, strain) is presented.
The effect of mechanochemical synthesis parameters (e.g., milling time, ball size) on structure is not explored in the supplied data.
